title: Åland: €14,350 a year, about 0.1 lung cancer deaths avoided a year (modelled)
markdown:
# Åland: €14,350 a year, about 0.1 lung cancer deaths avoided a year (modelled)

> About 0.1 deaths avoided a year (modelled) · €14,350 of €1M · €985,650 left: nothing more pays off on today's evidence

## The gap

Åland has too few lung cancer patients to compare: its 93 patients in five years are in the registry's national totals, but the registry does not publish care-path shares for the area [^model]. This page therefore cannot say how many Åland patients a year are missing from treatment that aims to cure. Nor can it say whether fewer are operated on or given radiotherapy that aims to cure [^model]. Instead of counting extra patients treated to cure, the plan ranks measures by deaths avoided [^model].

## The target

This plan is ranked by deaths avoided: about 0.1 a year (range 0.0–0.2), for €14,350 a year. [^model] Deaths avoided are modelled from stated assumptions, not observed. [^model]

## Funded actions

| # | Action and owner | Cost a year | Deaths avoided a year (range) | First step this week | Measure: today → target |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | **The county can start on Monday** | | | | |
| 1 | **Smoking cessation started at the first specialist visit**[^ev_smoking_cessation_at_diagnosis_1]. Chief physician and head nurse of pulmonology | €7,800 | 0.1 (0.0–0.1) | Write the standing order: every smoker with suspected lung cancer leaves the first visit with cessation medicine and a nurse call booked. | Share of smoking patients given cessation medicine at the first visit: not published today → 90% by 2027 |
| 2 | **Reflex molecular testing ordered by pathology**[^ev_reflex_molecular_1]. Chief pathologist together with the chief physician of oncology | €6,550 | 0.0 | The chief pathologist and the chief oncologist sign a standing order: every new non-small cell lung cancer sample goes to EGFR, ALK and PD-L1 testing the day it is diagnosed. | Days from tissue diagnosis to complete biomarker result; days to first drug treatment: not published today → 10 days by 2027 |
| | **Total** | **€14,350** | **0.1 (0.0–0.2)** | | |

Effects are modelled from published studies and stated assumptions, not observed here. Costs are assumptions. [^model]

## Needs a national decision (outside this budget)

- **Low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers**[^ev_ldct_screening_1]: Ministry of Social Affairs and Health and Palko (decision), Finnish Cancer Registry (steering), county (delivery). €112,508 a year; modelled to avoid 0.2 deaths a year (0.0–0.4). Not counted in this budget. Not a county decision. Ask the Ministry and Palko for the timetable after the 2026-2028 pilot and offer the county as a pilot site. [^model]

## What to measure from Monday

- Share of smoking patients given cessation medicine at the first visit: not published today → 90% by 2027. [^model]
- Days from tissue diagnosis to complete biomarker result; days to first drug treatment: not published today → 10 days by 2027. [^model]

## What more money buys, and what it cannot

EUR 14,350 a year funds every measure that adds deaths avoided in Åland [^model]. The remaining EUR 985,650 buys nothing more [^model]. Low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers needs a national decision [^model]. Lung cancer causes about 16 deaths a year in Åland [^deaths], and this plan is modelled to avoid 0.1 of them (range 0.01 to 0.19) [^model].

## Pilot ask

A six-month pilot of two actions: a chest surgeon reviews every decision not to operate, and every patient who cannot be operated is referred for precise radiotherapy. In six months that is about 8 new patients and 8 decisions reviewed. If our assumptions hold, about 0 of them (0 to 0) move to treatment that aims to cure in that time, and the share rises from 0.0% to 0.0% by 2028. The pilot replaces those assumptions with a count. [^model]

## Limits

- Effects are a range, not a probability: the lowest and highest results when every assumed effect size moves together from its low to its high bound [^model].
- No care-path shares are published for Åland [^model].
- 0 of 3 outcomes matched the estimated symptom-to-treatment clock in the expected direction beyond chance [^model].

draft_markdown:
## The gap
Åland has too few lung cancer patients to compare: its 93 patients in five years are in the registry's national totals, but the registry does not publish care-path shares for the area [^model]. This page therefore cannot say how many Åland patients a year are missing from treatment that aims to cure. Nor can it say whether fewer are operated on or given radiotherapy that aims to cure [^model]. Instead of counting extra patients treated to cure, the plan ranks measures by deaths avoided [^model].

## What more money buys, and what it cannot
EUR 14,350 a year funds every measure that adds deaths avoided in Åland. The remaining EUR 985,650 buys nothing more, because the 8 other measures cost more than the plan's limit of EUR 1,000,000 per death avoided a year [^model]. More would need a national decision on low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers [^model]. Lung cancer causes about 16 deaths a year in Åland [^deaths], and this plan is modelled to avoid 0.1 of them (range 0.01 to 0.19) [^model].

## Limits
- Effects are a range, not a probability: the lowest and highest results when every assumed effect size moves together from its low to its high bound [^model].
- No care-path shares are published for Åland, so nothing here is adjusted or compared, and county-level figures could not show cause in any case [^model].
- The plan does not use the estimated symptom-to-treatment clock: 0 of 3 measured outcomes matched it beyond chance [^model].
